title: Telemetry SDK: sampled-event reconciliation & graceful backfill plan for mixed-version clients
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description:
Background: We observe increasing skew between client-side SDK sampling logic and server-side ingestion expectations as multiple telemetry schema versions coexist. This leads to duplicate partial events, dropped reconciliation attempts, and gaps in backfilled analytics for customers upgrading incrementally. Goal: implement a safe, observable reconciliation and backfill strategy that lets newer backends tolerate sampled and partially-formed envelopes from older SDK/CLI/API clients, provide deterministic deduplication, and allow controlled backfilling without jeopardizing SLOs or storage costs.

Proposed design summary: 1) Sampled Envelope Metadata: require an opt-in light-weight reconciliation header (X-RW-Sample-Id / X-RW-Sample-Seq) propagated by SDK/CLI to identify sampled series. For legacy clients we will accept event fingerprints based on stable fields (client_id, route, timestamp-window) as a fallthrough. 2) Reconciliation Engine: ingestion service component that performs idempotent merge semantics: upsert-on-stable-key with last-writer-window and sequence-aware merge when Sample-Seq present. 3) Graceful Backfill Mode: an ingestion mode that tags backfill-origin events and routes them to a low-traffic path with TTL-based dedupe and cost-accounting. Backfill requests must supply a backfill manifest (S3 URL) and be rate-limited by tenant. 4) Sampling-aware Metrics: enrich telemetry commit logs with metadata to measure reconciliation rate, dedupe rate, and backfill amplification factor. 5) Compatibility Rules: maintain permissive parsing for at least two prior schema versions; enforce a rolling deprecation notice for clients older than 12 months.

Trade-offs considered: - Adding a sampling header increases SDK payload but simplifies correctness; we will implement as opt-in first to limit client churn. - Strongly consistent reconciliation would add coordination latency; we opt for eventual reconciliation with sequence windows to meet ingestion throughput targets. - Backfilling via a low-priority path increases storage overhead; mitigated via aggressive TTLs and explicit customer opt-in.

Rollout plan: Phase 0 (canary SDK): release opt-in SDK/CLI that emits Sample-Id and Sample-Seq; add parser and metrics in ingestion to accept headers. Phase 1 (ingest-only rollout): enable reconciliation engine in a single region for low-traffic tenants; run dedupe simulations against replay data. Phase 2 (controlled backfill): accept backfill manifests from internal ops and 3 pilot tenants; monitor amplification and SLO impact. Phase 3 (broad rollout): flip default SDK sampling header and publish deprecation timeline for old clients.

Acceptance criteria: - Deduplication reduces apparent duplicate event rate by >= 90% on canary tenants. - Ingestion tail latency at P99 increases by < 10% during reconciliation tests. - Backfill amplification factor (extra stored bytes / original bytes) < 1.4 for pilot tenants. - Observability: dashboards show reconciliation success rate, sample-id adoption, and per-tenant backfill cost.

QA and test plan: unit tests for header parsing and merge logic, integration tests with synthetic mixed-version traffic harness, replay-sim tests against 30 days of production telemetry in staging, and a safety kill-switch to disable reconciliation per-tenant.

Open questions: - Final header name and format (short binary vs ASCII UUID) to optimize SDK weight. - Backfill retention TTL policy and how it maps to pricing tiers. - Whether to expose reconciled-event provenance in Console UI for enterprise audits.

Artifacts and links: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Telemetry+Sampling+Reconciliation - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7283 - Ingest simulation harness: https://internal.redwood.ai/telemetry/sim-run/2026-02 - Dashboard mockup: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Telemetry/reconciliation-canary

Next steps: finalize header schema, implement ingestion parser and idempotent merge API, create canary SDK build and coordinate pilot tenants with Solutions Engineering.
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial triage meeting with product and Observability. Confirmed scope and success metrics.
2026-03-05: Spike completed for header encoding; ASCII UUID chosen for readability in logs. Prototype parser implemented in ingest-proxy branch.
2026-03-09: Reconciliation algorithm RFC reviewed by infra and runtime teams. Concern raised about sequence gaps; decided to use a windowed sequence reconciliation with tombstone markers.
2026-03-12: Integration test harness replayed 14 days of telemetry showing 72% duplicate reduction with prototype; further tuning needed to hit 90% target.
2026-03-14: Canary SDK build 0.1.0 published to internal package registry; preparing pilot tenant onboarding checklist.
